subject: english
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate idiom or phrase that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Mahesh has learnt **__not to take things seriously__**.

options.text: Your guess is as good as mine
Take it with a grain of salt

solution:
The correct answer is **"Take it with a grain of salt."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The phrase** "take it with a grain of salt"** means o view something with skepticism or not to take it too seriously.
 
• It suggests that the information may not be entirely accurate or reliable, and it advises the listener to approach it with a degree of skepticism.
 
• In other words, it encourages someone to not believe something too strongly or to be aware that there may be some level of uncertainty or doubt associated with the information.
 
 
• **Example**:* John heard a rumor about the new project, but he decided to **take it with a grain of salt**__.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the​ correct answer is Option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Your guess is as good as mine: **the speaker has no more information or knowledge about a particular topic than the person they are speaking to. (वक्ता के पास किसी विशेष विषय के बारे में उस व्यक्ति से अधिक जानकारी या ज्ञान नहीं है जिससे वह बात कर रहा है)
 
• **That's the last straw: **to convey that a particular event or situation is the final and intolerable occurrence, often leading to a decision or action. (यह बताना कि कोई विशेष घटना या स्थिति अंतिम और असहनीय घटना है, जो अक्सर किसी निर्णय या कार्रवाई की ओर ले जाती है)
 
• **Pull someone's leg: **to tease or joke with someone in a playful and light-hearted manner. (चंचल और हल्के-फुल्के अंदाज में किसी को चिढ़ाना या मजाक करना)
